opening_message:
Ticket 1: Maurice Perez (employee ID E036) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E036.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Maurice Perez (E036) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Source Code, which is at the maximum allowed level for a full-time employee. Recommending write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Maurice Perez (E036) is a contractor with basic security training (note says full-time; flagging discrepancy). Contractors with basic training max out at read. Requested write exceeds max, so recommending read.
reason: The two team notes conflict on employment type: HR indicates full-time Engineer (max for Source Code would allow write, since Engineer owns the system), but Security's database shows contractor with basic security training, and Security explicitly flags the discrepancy after verifying in their own DB. Under contractor policy, basic training caps access at read, and the requested write exceeds that max, so I grant the maximum allowed (read). Choosing the more restrictive verified record keeps access within policy.
